stem: Why are more adolescents living with chronic illness now than in the past?

options.text: It mainly reflects relabelling of normal adolescent variation as disease
It has remained essentially stable and clinicians are just noticing it more
It is rising because survival has improved, some conditions are truly more prevalent, and some conditions are appearing earlier
It mainly reflects short-term infectious illnesses now being counted as chronic disease
It is largely due to fewer adolescents growing out of minor allergic conditions

explanation: The correct answer is rising adolescent chronic illness. It is increasing because more young people survive long-term conditions, some diseases are genuinely more prevalent, and some conditions are presenting earlier in life.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the increase is not explained mainly by relabelling normal adolescent variation as disease.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the trend is not stable; chronic and disabling conditions in young people are increasing.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because the rise is driven by improved survival, true increases in prevalence, and earlier onset of some conditions.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because short-term infections are not what explains the rise in chronic illness.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this is not the main reason adolescent chronic illness is increasing.
